Nearly one in three Indian schools lacked internet access in the 2025–26 academic year. The Education Ministry’s UDISE+ report recorded internet facilities in 67.4% of schools. It lists 14,66,682 schools nationwide, with internet available in 9,89,191. That leaves 4,77,491 schools without it. Starlink could help connect remote schools and give teachers and students access to more learning resources. A child’s opportunities should not depend on whether a broadband cable reaches their classroom. Starlink has already connected more than 6 million students worldwide. This is another powerful reason to support Starlink in India. Media

Terence Tao: The mathematics in modern LLMs is fundamentally uncomplicated. Building and running them relies on linear algebra, matrix operations, and basic calculus, tools an undergraduate understands. We know how these systems function. The actual mystery lies elsewhere: why they excel at some tasks and stumble at others, and why we can't foresee that. We lack solid frameworks for predicting results across different domains, so discovery remains largely experimental. A central issue is how real-world information works. Pure noise has clean mathematics, perfectly ordered data has clean mathematics, but written language sits in between, structured yet noisy. Our math for that zone is limited, like how physics struggles at the middle scale between atomic and continuous scales. This gap means we can map out the parts but can't yet clarify sudden ability jumps or make solid domain-level predictions. That inconsistency, simple design versus hard-to-anticipate results, is the core riddle. Via Brian Keating's YouTube channel. Interested in AI? Follow @AiEvolutio58513 and never fall behind.
